results.title: Ophthalmic Technologies XXXVI, Conference Details
results.content: We present a novel in vivo human retina tracking platform leveraging high-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT) with circular scanning patterns to enable real-time, quantitative analysis of both smooth pursuit and visual acuity. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) offers high-speed, high signal-to-noise ratio, and volumetric retinal imaging, promising non-invasive detection of fine structural changes. This study introduces a computationally enhanced retinal OCT imaging approach that utilizes a complex CAC deconvolution filter to address both phase and amplitude errors, and integrates the CDS method for effective speckle suppression, enabling single-acquisition high-resolution volumetric retinal imaging. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a widely used imaging modality in ophthalmology for evaluating retinal structures, but it lacks vascular information critical for diagnosing diseases like diabetic retinopathy. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides noninvasive, micrometer-scale retinal imaging, yet clinical workflows face high scan volumes and interpretive variability. This study leverages the non-invasive imaging capabilities of optical coherence tomography (OCT) to characterize retinal degeneration in a USH2A KO rabbit model, aiming to establish OCT-derived biomarkers for both model characterization and therapeutic evaluation.

results.title: Advanced Biomedical and Clinical Diagnostic and Surgical ...
results.content: This submission discusses the development of an intraoperative platform that provides real-time assessment of the resection bed with a two-stage process: a rapid-scanning optical coherence tomography (OCT) handheld probe and a high-resolution multiphoton (NLO) and optical coherence microscopy (OCM) imaging module affixed to a semi-autonomous medical robot arm. Virtual pathology enables real-time, histology-like imaging of fresh tissue, offering a non-destructive alternative to FFPE and frozen section analysis for identifying positive surgical margins. We present a fully integrated, mobile stimulated Raman scattering imaging system that enables real-time, label-free assessment of brain tumor tissue. This study presents a novel spatial augmentation system that integrates real-time fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIm) with preoperative MRI navigation to enhance intraoperative guidance during brain tumor resection. The compact, energy-efficient sensor unit captures multimodal data—including intra-articular temperature, optical imaging, and light-scattering properties of synovial fluid—enabling real-time assessment of infection dynamics. We propose a multimodal imaging system that integrates optical coherence tomography (OCT), autofluorescence imaging (AFI), and photodynamic detection (PDD) to enable real-time monitoring of photodynamic therapy (PDT) in the oral cavity.
